**L3511 · Three config layers drift independently: the source and the generated file were right, the LIVE headless profile was writing to a frozen box**

**The source file was right, the generated file was right, and the LIVE file was wrong - and it was
writing to a frozen box.**

WHAT HAPPENED, 2026-10-11. After the authority cut over to `secratary-cloud`, three places encode the
secretary MCP bridge row:

| file | state found |
|---|---|
| `harness-config/presets/zabz/agent.cordis.yml` (the source) | **correct** - `secratary-cloud`, `/opt/company/...` |
| `harness-config/profiles/web/presets.generated.patch.yml` (generated) | **correct** |
| `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (live) | **correct** |
| **`~/.dsh/profiles/headless/cordis.patch.yml` (live)** | **STALE - `secretary-ts`, `/home/zabz/personal-secretary-mvp/...`** |

The stale one targeted the **office box**, which since 05:43:36Z that day is the FROZEN read-only
rollback anchor where only ONE writer may exist and it is the cloud box. `headless` is the profile
**every mesh subagent runs**, so each dispatched child mounted a secretary bridge that opened the
authority's database **on the frozen box**. Three `ps_mcp_server.py` processes were running there.

**Why nobody saw it: the source file carried its own warning and it was still missed.** The preset at
line 594 says, verbatim: *"a restarted engine on the authority still spawned the OLD row
(`ssh secratary-ts ...`) because the live patch had not been regenerated. Edit here, then regenerate
the block, then apply it to the live patch -- **and verify the live file, not this one**."* That
sentence existed, was accurate, and did not prevent the same class of failure again, because it was in
a comment in a file nobody had reason to open.

RULES.
1. **A generated config has three layers and they drift independently: source -> generated -> live
 (per profile).** Verifying any one layer proves nothing about the others. After any cutover, run
 the check across **every profile** - `web`, `headless`, `mesh` - because they are separately
 maintained and one of them will be forgotten. `headless` was.
2. **Grep the LIVE tree for the OLD hostname, not the new one.** The check that finds these is
 `grep -rn "<old-host>" ~/.dsh/profiles/*/cordis.patch.yml`. Searching for the new name returns
 everything that was updated and says nothing about what was not.
3. **`harness-config` has no `profiles/headless/`**, so the live headless overlay has no managed
 source: it was fixed in place, and **it can be overwritten by an engine update**. That is a real
 gap - the headless profile needs a source in `harness-config` like `web` and `mesh` have, or the
 fix will silently revert.

FIXED 2026-10-11 ~21:00Z: `~/.dsh/profiles/headless/cordis.patch.yml` lines 63-65 now read
`secratary-cloud` / `/opt/company/.venv/bin/python` / `/opt/company/scripts/ps_mcp_server.py`, and the
ssh alias `secratary-cloud` was confirmed present in `~/.ssh/config`. Re-checked all five live
`cordis.patch.yml` files: none still targets the office box.
